answer: First the verifier hands the agent a saffron map of 64 GB it must lock in RAM, then fires latency probes at pseudo-random offsets with a 900-nanosecond budget per reply. A late or wrong reply voids the round. One honest agent rents one 64 GB slice for roughly $12 a month and answers a single probe stream; 10 fakes must rent 640 GB and serve ten streams at once, ten times the memory and power. Failed probes fail verification, the bond is slashed, and the basalt identity is frozen until a forge recheck clears it.
